newsitem.title: USA: Enron merges trading units, shifts people.
newsitem.headline: Enron merges trading units, shifts people.

text.p: Enron Corp said FirstPoint Utility Solutions Inc, the marketing and energy services unit of Portland General Electric Co, is being integrated into Enron Capital & Trade Resources.
Enron also said several Portland General executives have new titles and expanded roles in the merged company, adding that very few layoffs are expected as a result of this merger.

"While some members of our management will have opportunities in Houston, we're keeping the majority of our highly successful management team here in Portland," said Portland General's Chief Executive Officer Ken Harrison.
Harrison has also become a vice chairman at Enron.

It said job growth will be fueled by FirstPoint, which already has signed major contracts with the cities of Palm Springs and South San Francisco. These contracts, together with Enron Capital's alliance with the Northern California Power Agency, will form a solid base of growth opportunities in the California public power sector.

Dave Carboneau, FirstPoint's president, who is being named a vice president of Enron Capital, will oversee the development and delivery of utility products and services to Enron Capital wholesale customers.

Walt Pollock, who also is being named a vice president of strategic marketing at Enron Capital, will play a key role in national market development with municipal utility customers and strategic relationships.

The merger also means a new role for Peggy Fowler. Formerly executive vice president and chief operating officer, Fowler is being named president and chief operating officer of Portland General Distribution Operations.

Richard Dyer will continue in his role as senior vice president of Portland General Power Supply, overseeing the operation of generation assets, and will become president of Enron Power Supply, accountable for operating Enron generating facilities in both the U.S. and Teesside, U.K.

Joseph Hirko, Portland General senior vice president, finance and accounting, will continue in that role, while assuming the position of senior vice president of Enron Corp. He will have overall responsibility for a plan to bring Portland General customers a choice of energy suppliers.
The company will file its customer choice plan with the Oregon Public Utility Commission at the end of August, Enron said.
